propositions: A push rejected by a pre-receive hook is unobservable on the async, library, and MCP write paths because stderr is discarded or unreachable by the caller, leaving the writer unaware of failure despite the contract that push never fails the caller.
A detached async push process spawned with Popen(stderr=DEVNULL, start_new_session=True) is never awaited, so all child warnings are lost to the OS; only OSError at spawn time is logged.
Library callers and MCP agents reading tool results never see the server-side stderr handler output; the MCP server writes to its own stderr while the agent reads only the structured result.

The remedy is a durable marker in the tracker's git dir recording terminal failures at the single _raise_if_strict choke point, exposed as rebar.push_status() for library embedders and as a push_status field on MCP write-tool results.

Recording is keyed to delivery failures only: commit-phase and transport failures are recorded because uncommitted writes are invisible upstream; non-failure reasons like push-disabled and remote-not-found are excluded to avoid false pending state in local-only stores.
